paper_title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to resolve ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, or textureless regions. To evaluate interactive reconstruction, we curate a challenging benchmark specifically designed to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods. Experiments show that Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click, improving performance on both standard and our curated benchmarks. Our results highlight that sparse human interaction provides an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Feed-forward stereo 3D reconstruction methods [44, 16, 29, 49] have transformed multi-view geometry by replacing iterative optimization [25, 34] with direct regression. Given two images, these models predict dense 3D pointmaps in single forward pass, achieving remarkable speed and generalization across diverse scenes. This paradigm has recently been extended to multi-view settings [42, 45, 53, 40, 3]. Despite their impressive performance, the efficiency comes at fundamental cost: when the prediction is wrong, there is no simple mechanism to correct it. Unlike optimizationbased methods [34] that iteratively refine their estimates using geometric constraints, feed-forward models produce single, irrevocable output and fail silently, particularly on challenging scenes with repetitive textures, symmetric structures, or extreme viewpoint changes (Fig. 1a,b). Several approaches aim to improve the reliability of feed-forward reconstruction models through test-time optimization [24, 5]. For instance, LoRA3D [24] introduces self-calibration pipeline that fine-tunes pretrained DUSt3R model [44] to target scene. Although these methods improve performance, iterative test-time optimization is computationally expensive and, more importantly, cannot resolve failures when the model encounters genuinely ambiguous scenes at inference time. Another line of work improves robustness by incorporating auxiliary geometric priors. For example, Pow3R [10] shows that conditioning on camera intrinsics, relative camera poses, or depth maps can significantly improve reconstruction performance. However, such auxiliary information is often unavailable in practice. Meanwhile, classical reconstruction methods have long relied on explicit Equal contribution. Unfortunately, automatically estimated correspondences remain unreliable in scenarios with repetitive textures or large viewpoint changes. Nevertheless, cross-view correspondences, even just handful of point pairs, carry powerful geometric information: they constrain the epipolar geometry, resolve depth ambiguities, and disambiguate symmetric structures. This motivates simple question: can sparse human-provided correspondences guide feed-forward 3D reconstruction models without sacrificing the efficiency of the feed-forward paradigm? Instead of relying solely on feed-forward models or automatically estimated correspondences, we allow the user to manually provide small set of cross-view point correspondences (Fig. 1a), when the model produces unsatisfactory reconstructions. To unlock this capability, we introduce CLICK3R, lightweight framework that incorporates userprovided correspondences into feed-forward 3D reconstruction, enabling interactive geometric correction without test-time model fine-tuning or optimization. Specifically, CLICK3R employs simple correspondence adapter that injects the geometric constraints imposed by user clicks into the reconstruction network via cross-attention mechanism  (Fig. 2)  . We train the base model and the adapter jointly end-to-end on widely used 3D datasets [28, 2, 57] using simulated human clicks. During training, the number of clicks is randomly sampled to expose the model to varying levels of user interaction, enabling it to operate under different levels of click sparsity at test time. To systematically evaluate the proposed interactive reconstruction, we further introduce Hard3DBench, benchmark designed to expose failure modes of state-of-the-art feed-forward reconstruction models. The benchmark contains image pairs and 5-view tuples with ground-truth 3D reconstructions, exhibiting challenging conditions (large viewpoint changes, low overlap, large baselines, extreme depth ranges) where feed-forward reconstruction models often struggle. Our experiments demonstrate that CLICK3R consistently outperforms baseline methods, particularly on challenging scenarios from Hard3DBench (Fig. 1c). Our contributions are summarized as follows: We propose CLICK3R, which injects sparse human correspondence clicks into feed-forward stereo 3D reconstruction networks via lightweight correspondence adapter. We curate Hard3DBench, diagnostic benchmark with detailed failure taxonomy under which current feed-forward reconstruction models degrade substantially relative to standard evaluation samples. We show that CLICK3R dramatically improves reconstruction accuracy on challenging cases. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work on interactive stereo feed-forward 3D reconstruction using sparse correspondence clicks.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Feed-Forward Stereo 3D Reconstruction. DUSt3R [44] pioneered dense 3D pointmap regression from image pairs using CroCo-pretrained [48, 47] ViT encoder-decoder, bypassing explicit matching and triangulation. MASt3R [16] extended this with dense local feature heads. The paradigm has rapidly advanced toward multi-view: Spann3R [41] and MUSt3R [3] use spatial memory across frames; CUT3R [43] employs recurrent model with persistent state; Fast3R [53] scales to 1000+ images in single forward pass; and VGGT [42] and Pi3 [45] predict from arbitrary views with single Transformer. Despite their diversity, all these methods rely solely on learned visual priors and cannot incorporate external geometric evidence at inference. Our work is orthogonal: CLICK3R augments feed-forward stereo reconstruction with sparse correspondence guidance. Conditioned 3D Reconstruction. Several concurrent methods condition feed-forward 3D models on external geometric signals: Pow3R [10] on camera intrinsics, depth, or pose, G-CUT3R [14] on camera and depth modalities, Rig3R [17] on multi-camera rig metadata, and Mono3R [18] on monocular depth. MapAnything [13] unifies flexible mix of conditioning inputs (intrinsics, poses, depth, partial reconstructions) into single feed-forward model, while Any4D [12] extends conditional reconstruction to dynamic 4D scenes with multi-modal sensor inputs. In the depth estimation domain, PromptDA [21] prompts Depth Anything [54] with sparse LiDAR points. All these methods condition on scene-level priors that improve metric accuracy but cannot resolve perceptual aliasing. To our knowledge, CLICK3R is the first to introduce correspondence prompting, which conditions feedforward 3D reconstruction on cross-view point correspondences that directly disambiguate geometric ambiguities, analogous to SAMs [15, 27] click-based segmentation prompting. Interactive Vision System. Interactive segmentation has long history of incorporating user guidance into visual recognition. Early methods use bounding boxes [30] or scribbles [20], while recent approaches adopt click-based prompting [51, 4, 23, 39], culminating in SAM [15, 27]. Beyond segmentation, point-based interaction has been extended to image editing: DragGAN [26] and DragDiffusion [37] enable users to manipulate content by dragging points. Recent work has also explored interactive guidance for 3D reconstruction; for example, Toon3D [46] uses sparse user annotations for cartoon 3D reconstruction. However, these interactive paradigms have largely remained confined to 2D tasks or stylized 3D settings. Early interactive systems also explored correspondence-based 3D reconstruction [9]. CLICK3R brings this idea to feed-forward stereo models, with point correspondences as geometric constraints rather than semantic cues.

sections.title: 3.3 Point Correspondence Adapter
sections.content: We inject correspondence information into DUSt3Rs decoder using two-way attention adapter inspired by SAM [15], enabling bidirectional exchange between sparse correspondence tokens and dense image tokens (Figure 2). Two-Way Attention. The adapter has = 2 layers. Each layer applies: (1) self-attention over prompt tokens Tv; (2) prompt-to-image cross-attention, Attn(Tv, Gv, Gv); (3) an MLP on prompt tokens; and (4) image-to-prompt cross-attention, Attn(Gv, Tv, Tv). This bidirectional design lets prompts condition image features with correspondence constraints while allowing prompt tokens to absorb local visual context. Image Positional Encoding. sections.title: 4 Hard3DBench
sections.content: The primary value of CLICK3R is on challenging scenarios where DUSt3R fails. Standard evaluations report only aggregate metrics, masking catastrophic failures on geometrically ambiguous scenes. To enable systematic analysis, we introduce Hard3DBench, curated benchmark for both 2-view stereo and 5-view multi-view settings, accompanied by failure taxonomy that exposes the specific failure modes of feed-forward 3D reconstruction. The 2-view setting contains 404 in-distribution and 300 out-of-distribution pairs, and the 5-view setting 400 in-distribution and 300 out-of-distribution tuples. In-distribution samples come from held-out test/validation splits of four datasets used to train DUSt3R and CLICK3R: BlendedMVS [56], CO3D [28], Habitat [32], and WildRGB-D [50]. Out-of-distribution samples come from five datasets absent from training: 7Scenes [38], DTU [11], ETH3D [35], NRGBD [1], and ScanNet [6]. Full curation details are in Appendix C. Failure Taxonomy. sections.title: 5.2 Evaluation on Standard Benchmark
sections.content: Table 1 presents results on standard benchmarks. Without prompts, CLICK3R performs on par with DUSt3R (retrained). Adding even single well-chosen prompt (1p_best5) consistently improves over the unprompted baseline. The grid oracle reveals substantially larger headroom, with striking +8.5% mAA@30 on ARKitScenes (from 84.27% to 92.75%). This confirms that prompt location matters significantly: the model can leverage even single correspondence to meaningfully reduce pose error when placed in the right region. Notably, the grid oracle delivers the largest pose gains while pointmap error improves only modestly, indicating that prompts primarily reshape the overall scene configuration rather than uniformly tightening local surface fits.

sections.title: 5.3 Evaluation on Hard3DBench
sections.content: Table 2 reports results on both the 2-view and 5-view subsets. CLICK3R consistently improves mAA@30 over the retrained DUSt3R baseline across all four conditions, with the largest gain of +9.9 on the 5-view in-distribution split, and pointmap error also improving in all four conditions. Notably, these improvements are obtained without increasing input resolution or training data. These results suggest that even sparse correspondence prompts effectively resolve failure modes in highly ambiguous scenes, enabling the model to recover accurate geometry where fully automatic methods struggle. sections.title: 5.4 Evaluation with Human-Labeled Correspondences
sections.content: The previous experiments use ground-truth correspondences derived from known 3D geometry. To evaluate CLICK3R under realistic annotation conditions, we test on 100 image pairs with humanlabeled correspondences. The pairs are drawn from out-of-distribution set of Hard3DBench and cover challenging geometric configurations. human annotator, not specifically familiar with the evaluated datasets or scenes, freely chooses sparse correspondences (3.8 per pair on average, from 1 to 7) via labeling interface (Figure 12), without access to ground-truth depth or camera parameters. Table 3 demonstrates that human-provided prompts drastically reduce median rotation error compared to the unprompted model (8.78 vs. 17.30) and raise mAA@30 from 36.2 to 56.2, along with significant improvement in Relative Rotation Accuracy. Compared to the random ground-truth oracle (K = 4), human labels recover about 96% of the medRRE improvement gap, showing that sparse, imperfect human clicks capture most of the benefit of perfect correspondences. These results confirm that CLICK3R translates effectively from synthetic oracle prompts to practical human interaction.

sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.content: We presented CLICK3R, an interactive stereo 3D reconstruction framework that bridges fully automatic feed-forward methods, correspondence-based classical pipelines, and recent prompt-based vision systems. By injecting sparse point correspondences into feed-forward stereo 3D reconstruction model through lightweight correspondence adapter, CLICK3R enables users to guide the reconstruction process without test-time model fine-tuning or optimization, resolving geometric ambiguities that often cause catastrophic failures. Experiments on our curated Hard3DBench demon9 strate that even handful of correspondences can dramatically improve reconstruction quality in challenging scenarios. While CLICK3R has limitations (Appendix J) and failure cases (Appendix H), we hope this work inspires further exploration of correspondence prompting as promising direction for interactive 3D reconstruction, analogous to how SAM [15] advanced interactive prompting for 2D segmentation.

sections.title: Supplementary Material
sections.content: We provide implementation details and training configuration (Section A), details on Hard3DBench construction (Section C), per-category analysis on the 2-view subset (Section D), additional experiments including training strategy ablation on all evaluation sets, stricter pose thresholds, prompt count ablation, augmentation robustness, incorrect prompts, automatic prompts, MASt3R transfer, and error distribution analysis (Section E), an internal analysis of how the correspondence adapter modifies encoder features and decoder attention (Section F), additional qualitative results (Section G), failure case analysis (Section H), licenses of the existing assets we use (Section I), limitation (Section J), and broader impacts (Section K).

sections.title: A Implementation Details
sections.content: CLICK3R follows the DUSt3R [44] training recipe (loss function, optimizer, data augmentation, symmetric batching) and inherits its CroCo v2 [47] ViT-Large encoder and dual asymmetric decoder. Below we detail the components specific to CLICK3R. Correspondence adapter. We insert two SAM-style [15] Two-Way Transformer adapters (depth 2, 8 heads, MLP dim 2048, embedding dim 768) between the encoder and decoder (Section 3.3). The two adapters share single correspondence tokenizer (Section 3.2) that encodes each correspondence point as the sum of positional encoding (random Fourier features [15]), an image identity embedding, and pair identity embedding (vocabulary size 256). When prompts are provided, the adapted features replace the encoder output; otherwise, the adapter is bypassed and the model reduces to standard DUSt3R. The adapters and tokenizer are randomly initialized; all other weights are initialized from the CroCo pretrained checkpoint. All parameters are trained jointly end-to-end. Training data. We train on nine datasets, each contributing 100,000 image pairs: BlendedMVS [56], MegaDepth [19], CO3D [28], StaticThings3D [36], Waymo Open [52], ARKitScenes [2], WildRGBD [50], Habitat [32], and ScanNet++ [57]. Validation uses held-out splits from six of these datasets with 1,000 pairs each. Ground-truth prompt generation. During training, correspondence prompts are generated by projecting view 1s 3D pointmap into view 2 and accepting correspondences where the 3D distance to the nearest view 2 surface point is below 5 cm (which implicitly rejects occluded points). Per sample, 30% receive zero prompts (adapter bypassed), 40% receive 14, and 30% receive 512 correspondences. Training configuration. We train for 100 epochs on 4 GPUs with per-GPU batch size 16, using AdamW (β1=0.9, β2=0.95, weight decay 0.05), learning rate of 104 with 10 epochs of linear warmup followed by cosine decay to 106, and float16 mixed precision. Baseline image preprocessing. DUSt3R-family models (DUSt3R, MASt3R, CLICK3R) use images normalized to [1, 1]. The VGGT and Pi3 wrappers internally denormalize images to [0, 1] before forwarding to match each models expected input range. Standard benchmark data. The held-out splits are the CO3D test sequences, the ScanNet++ validation scenes, and the ARKitScenes validation videos, each processed with the DUSt3R pipeline. Evaluation metric details. The scale-and-shift-invariant pointmap error uses the normalization of DUSt3R: we divide the predicted pointmap by its mean point distance, shift both pointmaps by their median depth, and rescale the prediction to the median distance of the ground-truth points to their median point. We then average the per-pixel L2 distance over all valid pixels (i.e., L2 within each 3D point, mean across pixels). For mAA@θ, relative camera pose is first estimated from each models predicted pointmaps via PnP-RANSAC (cv2.solvePnPRansac with the SQPNP solver), recovering per-view camera-to-world poses. Rotation error is the geodesic distance arccos(cid:0)(tr(R gtRpred) 1)/2(cid:1) in degrees; translation error is the angular deviation between predicted and ground-truth translation directions, with sign ambiguity handled by min(α, 180 α). mAA@θ is the area under 14 Table 4: Runtime and model complexity. sections.title: B Training Details
sections.content: Generating Training Correspondences. During training, we generate prompts from ground-truth 3D geometry. For each image pair with known cameras and pointmaps, we first sample the number of correspondence prompts according to curriculum: 30% of samples use no prompts (K = 0), 40% use small number of prompts (K [1, 4]), and 30% use more prompts (K [5, 12]). Given the sampled value of K, we: (1) sample 3D points from the first view; (2) project them into both views using known intrinsics and extrinsics; (3) retain only points that are mutually visible, verified by comparing the projected 3D position against the second views GT pointmap within distance threshold. Training Protocol. We initialize from CroCo v2 [47] pretrained weights and train all parameters end-to-end, including both the base model and the adapter. Training uses 4 GPUs, AdamW (lr = 104) with linear warmup and cosine decay. We train on the same dataset mixture as DUSt3R: CO3D [28], ARKitScenes [2], ScanNet++ [57], WildRGB-D [50], BlendedMVS [56], MegaDepth [19], Habitat [32], Waymo [52], and StaticThings3D [36] (100K pairs each), at 224 224 resolution. With batch size 16 per GPU on A100s, training step takes 0.60 for CLICK3R and 0.55 for DUSt3R (retrained), which amounts to about 234 and 215 hours for 100 epochs on 4 GPUs, with peak memory of 29,069 and 28,731 MiB per GPU. Hard3DBench Details Hard3DBench has two subsets: 2-view stereo subset of 404 in-distribution and 300 out-ofdistribution pairs, and 5-view multi-view subset of 400 in-distribution and 300 out-of-distribution tuples. Both subsets use pretrained DUSt3Rs pose error as the difficulty signal, rather than CLICK3R or our retrained baseline, so the benchmark is defined independently of the methods under evaluation. They share the same source datasets: the in-distribution split uses held-out test/val splits of four DUSt3R training datasets, while the out-of-distribution split uses five datasets entirely absent from training (Table 6 reports the 2-view per-dataset statistics). DTU uses the cameras of MVSNet [55] and the depth maps rendered by Spann3R [41], 7Scenes depth is registered to the color camera as in SimpleRecon [33], ScanNet is prepared following MonST3R [58], and ETH3D following Pi3 [45]. 2-view subset. To obtain hard cases, we evaluate the pretrained DUSt3R model on up to 20,000 randomly drawn image pairs per dataset (69K in-distribution, 68K out-of-distribution), prefiltering pairs with insufficient co-visibility via depth reprojection in DUSt3Rs 224224 crop space. sections.title: H Failure Cases
sections.content: Figure 14 shows four representative failure modes of CLICK3R. Each panel shows the input image pair (left), the ground-truth reconstruction (middle), and the CLICK3R reconstruction with clicks (right). (a) Few overlap. When the two views share little or no visual overlap, the model must hallucinate the relative geometry from appearance alone. In this ScanNet++ example the views observe disjoint 22 Figure 11: How prompts reshape decoder cross-attention. Each row shows query patch in view 1 (green cross) and its decoder cross-attention map over view 2. Without prompts (middle), attention is diffuse. With = 8 prompts (right, cyan dots), attention concentrates on the correct corresponding region. parts of room; comparing the ground truth with the CLICK3R output reveals severely misaligned reconstruction. Without co-visible content, correspondence clicks cannot anchor the two viewsthis is fundamental limitation of pairwise reconstruction. (b) Heavy rotation. Extreme viewpoint changes (> 90) remain an unsolved challenge. In this ARKitScenes pair, the CLICK3R reconstruction remains geometrically distorted compared to the ground truth. While clicks can reduce error in moderate-rotation cases  (Table 7)  , very heavy rotations overwhelm the models capacity to reconcile drastically different visual appearances. (c) Large-scale scenes. For outdoor scenes with large spatial extent (MegaDepth), correspondence clicks correctly constrain geometry near the clicked regions, but distant structures still exhibit bending and deformationvisible here as warped sky and distorted building facades far from the click locations. small number of clicks cannot regularize the entire scene when the depth range spans tens of meters. 23 Figure 12: screenshot of the labeling tool we build to harness human labeled correspondences. (d) Ambiguous correspondences. On textureless or repetitive surfaces, correspondences themselves become ambiguous. In this ARKitScenes bathroom scene with featureless marble walls and white surfaces, click on one location is visually indistinguishable from many others, providing little geometric information. The CLICK3R reconstruction remains distorted compared to the ground truth, and clicks offer negligible improvement.

sections.title: J Limitations
sections.content: Although correspondence prompts are ideally injected into frozen pretrained model, we find that training the base model [44] end-to-end with the adapter is necessary in practice, incurring nontrivial training cost. Partly due to this cost, our experiments focus on two-view reconstruction; extending to multi-view models [45, 42, 53, 40] with trajectory prompts across views is an important direction. Architecturally, the adapter treats correspondences as soft feature conditioning via cross-attention rather than enforcing hard geometric constraints. Although eight correspondences suffice to determine relative pose algebraically [8], the adapter cannot replicate such reasoning: it modulates all image tokens through learned attention at single injection point, and this signal is progressively diluted across twelve subsequent decoder cross-attention blocks. Deeper injection at multiple decoder layers and explicit geometric reasoning modules may be worth future inquiry to help close this gap. Finally, due to computational constraints, the model is trained only at resolution of 224px in stereo setting, although it has demonstrated multi-view capability through global alignment. In addition, prompts must be co-visible in both views, so the two inputs need shared visible region; non-overlapping inputs could be connected through intermediate views by chaining correspondences. sections.title: K Broader Impacts
sections.content: Our work enables more efficient 3D reconstruction from sparse user-provided correspondences. By allowing small number of clicks to anchor pairwise reconstruction, CLICK3R can lower the barrier to 3D capture in diverse, in-the-wild scenes, which may benefit downstream applications such as robotics, AR/VR content creation, and scientific imaging where dense ground-truth geometry is unavailable. Our model and benchmark are built from publicly available datasets (CO3D, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes, BlendedMVS, MegaDepth, Habitat, WildRGB-D, Waymo, and standard evaluation benchmarks), and therefore do not raise privacy concerns. While our algorithm itself is scene-agnostic and does not introduce explicit bias, the underlying training datasets may reflect societal or geographic biases present in the source data (e.g., predominantly indoor scenes from North American buildings, or object categories skewed toward consumer products).
